doc: Trust is capability-scoped, not identity-scoped: a role may be excellent at a task and still hold low authority. A workflow step grants the level; a role declares the maximum it may ever be granted. The effective level is min(role.max_trust, step.trust). Nothing in a task prompt can raise it.

levels.name: read_only
may: read any repository file
read beads, git history, docs, knowledge base
run read-only inspection commands (git log, git diff, mix help, bd show, kb query)
report findings in the run transcript
may_not: run commands that mutate a database, container or remote service

levels.name: draft_artifacts
may: create and update artifacts under .agents/ (research notes, RFCs, architecture maps, task graphs, evaluation reports)
create beads and add discovered-from links
append project-memory records
propose diffs as text without applying them
may_not: modify apps/, config/, design/, scripts/ or any product source
modify gates, evaluators, CI or the constitution

levels.name: sandbox_mutation
levels.summary: Change code in an isolated workspace.
may: modify product source inside a git worktree or feature branch
create and run tests
run the full local gate lanes
start and stop local dev services and containers
may_not: modify any evaluator, benchmark or holdout used to judge this run

levels.name: branch_integration
levels.summary: Land work on a shared branch.
may: commit to the session's feature branch
merge --no-ff into develop
push branches to origin
close beads
regenerate client adapters
may_not: change gate definitions or CI workflow files

levels.name: protected_change
levels.summary: Change what protects the project. Requires an explicit gate.
may: merge to main and cut a release
modify gate definitions, CI workflows and scripts/ci-local.sh
modify evaluators, benchmarks and holdouts
promote an evolution candidate
run production database migrations
requires: an explicit grant in the workflow step, not an inherited default
a separate reviewer role that did not author the change
the full gate lane green, with evidence attached

levels.name: administrative
levels.summary: Credentials, infrastructure, irreversible external action. Human-only by default.
may: rotate or issue credentials
change infrastructure outside the repository (DNS, R2 buckets, database plans)
delete remote data or history
publish to an external registry or a public surface
requires: explicit human authorisation recorded in the bead for this specific action
no agent may hold T5 by role; it is granted per action or not at all

escalation.doc: An agent that needs an action above its level stops and emits a BLOCKED report naming the action, the level it requires and the role or human that holds it. It does not ask another agent to perform the action on its behalf.
